termDefinitions.meaningEn: Event time is when something actually happened in the real world, as opposed to when the system processed it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记事件时间已经推进到哪里的信号，用于判断何时能安全关窗。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watermark signals how far event time has progressed, used to decide when it's safe to close a window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析的列式数据库，优化跨大量行的聚合查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLAP is a columnar analytical database optimized for aggregation queries across many rows.

scenario: 广告点击聚合器的写入量峰值达到 1 万次/秒，远超广告主的查询负载。
scenario_en: The ad click aggregator has a peak write load of 10k clicks per second, far above advertiser query load.
q: 这套设计对应哪个系统设计模式？为什么？
q_en: Which system design pattern does this design match, and why?
options: 扩展读模式：广告主的查询流量远多于写入流量
需要跨节点强一致的分布式事务模式
扩展写模式：写入量远超读负载，整套架构都为高写吞吐服务
面向内容关键词匹配的全文检索模式
why: 写入量（点击）远超读取量（广告主查询）；Kafka 缓冲、Flink 预聚合、按 AdId 分区都是「扩展写」模式的标准动作。
why_en: Click writes dwarf advertiser query reads, and the whole architecture — stream buffering, pre-aggregation, AdId partitioning — is textbook scaling-writes.
options_en: Scaling-reads pattern: advertiser query traffic far outnumbers write traffic
A pattern requiring cross-node strongly-consistent distributed transactions
Scaling-writes pattern: write volume dwarfs read load, and the whole architecture serves high write throughput
A full-text search pattern built around keyword matching

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计模式，核心矛盾是写入量远超读取量，架构围绕吸收高写吞吐展开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scaling writes is a system-design pattern where write volume far exceeds read volume, and the architecture is built around absorbing that write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据按某个 key（比如 AdId）拆到多个节点，换取并行处理能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning splits data across multiple nodes by a key like AdId to enable parallel processing.

optionExplanations: 读写比例的方向说反了：本题恰恰是写入远多于读取。
本题所有组件都是最终一致，没有用到跨节点强一致事务。
点击（写）远远压过广告主查询（读），从消息队列缓冲到实时预聚合再到按广告分区，整套设计都在为扛住写入吞吐服务。
系统里没有对点击内容做关键词检索的需求，全文检索能力跟这套架构无关。
optionExplanations_en: This has the read/write ratio backwards — writes vastly outnumber reads here.
Every component in this design is eventually consistent; there's no cross-node strong-consistency transaction in play.
Writes (clicks) massively outnumber reads (advertiser queries); buffering the stream, aggregating early, and partitioning by ad ID are all moves that scale for heavy writes.
There's no keyword-search need on click content anywhere in this system, so full-text search isn't relevant to this architecture.

q: 把「最优方案」中一次点击从发生到可查询的路径排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put one click's path from occurrence to queryability in the correct order:
steps: Flink 按 AdId + 分钟窗口实时聚合
用户在网页上点击广告
聚合结果写入 OLAP 分析库
Click Processor 接到 /click 请求并处理
广告主查询 OLAP，拿到近实时指标
事件被写入 Kafka / Kinesis 流
why: 点击 → 处理服务 → 流 → 流处理器聚合 → OLAP → 查询，这条链就是最终架构的主动脉，必须能脱口而出。
why_en: A click flows from the browser to the click processor, into the stream, through Flink aggregation, into the OLAP store, and finally to the advertiser's query.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["用户点击广告"] --> P["Click Processor"] P --> K["Kafka / Kinesis"] K --> F["Flink 实时聚合
AdId + 分钟"] F --> O["OLAP 分析库"] O --> A["广告主查询"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收 /click 请求、处理点击事件的无状态服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Click Processor is the stateless service that receives /click requests and handles click events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息流平台，提供可重放的持久化事件日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka and Kinesis are distributed streaming platforms that provide a replayable, durable event log.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流式处理框架，支持事件时间窗口聚合和状态管理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework that supports event-time windowed aggregation and state management.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析查询优化的列式数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLAP databases use columnar storage optimized for analytical aggregation queries.

scenario: 点击处理服务本身要扛住每秒上万次的 /click 请求。
scenario_en: The click processing service itself must handle about 10k /click requests per second.
q: 这一层怎么扩展？
q_en: How should the click processing layer scale?
options: 垂直升级单机配置硬扛
水平扩多实例 + 负载均衡，用云自动伸缩
换用更快的编程语言重写
把服务放到 CDN 边缘执行
options_en: Vertically upgrade a single box and tough it out.
Scale out with more instances behind a load balancer, using cloud autoscaling.
Rewrite it in a faster programming language.
Run the service at the CDN edge.
why: 无状态服务的标准扩法：多实例水平扩容、负载均衡分流，云厂商的托管自动伸缩按 CPU/内存指标增减实例。
why_en: The click processor scales horizontally behind a load balancer, with managed autoscaling adding instances based on CPU or memory.
tradeoff: 水平扩容的弹性 vs 垂直升级的简单直接
whenOtherWins: 流量很小或原型阶段，单实例最简单；垂直扩容也能顶一阵，但有硬件上限且是单点。
optionExplanations: 垂直升级有硬件上限，扛不住上万 QPS 的持续增长，而且始终是单点。
这是无状态服务的标准打法：起更多实例、前面挂负载均衡分流，云平台的自动伸缩组再按 CPU 或内存使用率动态增减机器数。
换语言优化单机吞吐填不平数量级缺口，解决不了扩展模型问题。
CDN 缓存静态内容，不能替代写路径上要处理业务逻辑的服务。
optionExplanations_en: Vertical scaling hits a hardware ceiling and stays a single point of failure — it can't keep up with sustained tens-of-thousands QPS.
This is the standard playbook for a stateless service: add more instances, put a balancer in front to spread traffic, and let managed auto-scaling add or remove instances based on CPU and memory.
A faster language might squeeze more out of one machine, but it can't close an order-of-magnitude gap — that's not a scaling model fix.
A CDN caches static content — it can't stand in for a service that has to execute write-path business logic.

scenario: Kinesis 单个 shard 的写入上限是 1MB/s 或 1000 条记录/s；系统要扛住 1 万次点击/秒的峰值写入。
scenario_en: A single Kinesis shard supports 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s, and the system must handle a 10k clicks-per-second peak.
q: 这条写入上限对分片设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this write limit imply for shard design?
options: 1 万/秒峰值必须并行开 10 个以上分片
单个分片吞吐可以无限扩容，不用分片
只要开了自动扩缩容，就不用关心分片数
分片数量只影响成本，不影响吞吐上限
options_en: At a 10k/sec peak you need ten or more shards in parallel.
A single shard scales without limit, so no sharding is needed.
With autoscaling on you never have to think about shard count.
Shard count only affects cost, not the throughput ceiling.
why: 1MB/s 或 1000 条/s 是单分片硬上限；1 万/秒的峰值必然超出单分片承载力，必须并行开至少 10 个以上分片分摊写入。
why_en: A Kinesis shard caps at 1MB/s or 1,000 records/s, so a 10k-per-second peak requires spreading writes across at least ten shards in parallel.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的分布式流式数据服务，功能类似 Kafka。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis is AWS's managed distributed streaming service, similar in role to Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kinesis 流的分区单位，每个分片有独立的吞吐上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is a partition of a Kinesis stream, and each shard has its own throughput cap.

optionExplanations: 题目给的这条硬上限意味着单分片扛不住 1 万/秒的峰值，缺口只能靠并行铺开至少 10 个以上分片来摊薄这份写入。
Kinesis 分片有明确的写入上限，不是可以无限扩容的资源。
自动扩缩容管的是实例数或资源规格，管不了单分片的硬性吞吐上限，分片数依然要按峰值算清楚。
分片数量直接决定能扛住多少写入吞吐，不只是成本高低的问题。
optionExplanations_en: That per-shard ceiling means a 10k/s peak can't land on a single shard — the only way to close the gap is fanning writes out across at least ten-plus shards running in parallel.
Kinesis shards have a hard write-throughput ceiling — they aren't a resource you can scale without limit.
Auto-scaling adjusts instance count or resource size; it can't lift a single shard's hard throughput cap, so shard count still has to be sized against peak load.
Shard count directly determines how much write throughput you can sustain, not just how much you pay.

scenario: 流需要分片以支撑 1 万/秒；下游 Flink 希望各分片可以独立并行消费，同一广告的计数不跨分片。
scenario_en: The stream must be sharded for 10k clicks per second; downstream Flink should consume shards independently without splitting one ad's counts across shards.
q: 流的分片键选什么？
q_en: What should the stream partition key be?
options: 用随机 UUID，追求最均匀分布
按点击者的 UserId 分片求均匀
按事件时间戳分片，天然有序
按 AdId：同广告事件同分片，可并行
options_en: Use a random UUID for the most even spread.
Shard by the clicking user's UserId for evenness.
Shard by event timestamp so data stays ordered.
Shard by AdId: one ad's events land together and consume in parallel.
why: 按 AdId 分片让同一广告的所有事件天然汇聚到一处，Flink 各任务独立聚合各自分片，无需跨分片协调。
why_en: Sharding by ad ID keeps all events for one ad in the same shard so stream processors can consume shards independently in parallel.
tradeoff: 聚合局部性（同广告同分片）vs 写入的绝对均匀分布
whenOtherWins: 出现爆款热广告时，纯 AdId 分片会造出热分片——那时要给热门广告的 key 追加随机后缀进一步打散。
optionExplanations: 随机 UUID 追求均匀分布，但同一广告的事件会散落到多个分片，破坏了聚合的局部性。
用户和广告是不同维度，按 UserId 分片同样会让同一广告的事件分散到多个分片。
事件到达时间和广告归属无关，按时间戳分片一样打散了同一广告的数据。
同一广告的事件天然落进同一个分片，各个 Flink 任务只处理自己那一份，彼此不用商量，也不需要跨分片协调。
optionExplanations_en: Random UUIDs spread writes evenly, but events for the same ad end up scattered across shards, breaking aggregation locality.
User and ad are different dimensions — sharding by UserId still scatters one ad's events across multiple shards.
Arrival time has nothing to do with which ad an event belongs to, so time-based sharding scatters the same ad's data too.
Events tied to the same ad all funnel into one shard, so each Flink task works its own shard on its own, with zero cross-shard coordination needed.

scenario: 点击流按 AdId 分成 N 个分片，峰值 1 万点击/秒，聚合吞吐要随分片数一起涨。
scenario_en: The click stream is split into N shards by AdId at 10k clicks/sec, and aggregation throughput has to grow with shard count.
q: 流处理层（Flink）如何随分片数扩展？
q_en: How does the Flink layer scale with the number of shards?
options: 单个全局任务串行读所有分片
靠数据库锁协调多个消费者
每个分片配一个 Flink 任务并行聚合
无法扩展，只能垂直加内存
options_en: One global task reads all shards serially.
Coordinate consumers with database locks.
One Flink task per shard, each aggregating its shard in parallel.
It can't scale; you can only add more memory.
why: 分片之间相互独立，所以 Flink 天然可以按分片并行：一个分片一个任务，各算各的 AdId 聚合。
why_en: Flink scales horizontally by running a separate job or task per shard, each aggregating the ad IDs in its own shard.
optionExplanations: 单任务串行读全部分片会让吞吐被单线程封顶，违背了分片独立并行的设计初衷。
数据库锁不是流处理框架的扩展手段，锁本身反而会成为新的瓶颈。
分片之间相互独立，Flink 天然可以一分片配一个任务并行处理，任务数随分片数线性扩展。
纵向加内存有硬件上限，最终还是会封顶，不是真正的扩展路径。
optionExplanations_en: Reading all shards serially in one task caps throughput at a single thread, defeating the point of independent shards.
A database lock isn't how a stream framework scales — the lock itself would just become a new bottleneck.
Shards are independent, so Flink naturally runs one task per shard in parallel, and task count scales linearly with shard count.
Adding memory vertically hits a hardware ceiling eventually — it isn't a real scaling path.

scenario: 自建 ClickHouse 做分析库；广告主打开后台通常一次要看自己名下所有广告的汇总视图。
scenario_en: You run ClickHouse yourself as the analytics store, and advertisers usually open a dashboard showing all ads under their account.
q: 分析库按什么分片？
q_en: How should the analytics database be sharded?
options: 按 AdvertiserId：账户查询单节点
按分钟级的时间戳分片，写入最均匀
按点击者的 UserId 分片保均匀
把数据完全随机打散到各节点
options_en: Shard by AdvertiserId so account queries hit one node.
Shard by minute-level timestamp for the most even writes.
Shard by the clicking user's UserId to stay balanced.
Scatter the data completely at random across nodes.
why: 查询模式是「一个广告主看自己全部广告」，按 AdvertiserId 分片让这类查询单节点即可完成；同时要持续监控查询性能是否满足 SLA。
why_en: Sharding the OLAP store by advertiser ID colocates each advertiser's data so account-wide queries stay on a single node.
tradeoff: 账户级查询局部性 vs 写入分布的绝对均匀度
whenOtherWins: 用 Snowflake / BigQuery 等托管仓库时无法（也无需）手动控制数据放置，扩展交给平台，你只需要盯查询 SLA。

termDefinitions.meaning: 自建的开源列式 OLAP 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ClickHouse is a self-hosted open-source columnar OLAP database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识广告主账户的主键，用于聚合同一账户下所有广告的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AdvertiserId identifies an advertiser account, used to group all of that account's ad data.

optionExplanations: 广告主打开后台通常要看自己名下全部广告的汇总，用 AdvertiserId 做分片依据，这类查询一台节点就能兜住。
按分钟时间戳分片跟「按账户查全部」的查询模式不对齐，同一广告主的数据仍会跨多个分片。
UserId 是点击者维度，跟广告主账户视图无关，同样打散不了这类查询。
完全随机打散没有任何局部性可言，账户级查询要扫遍所有分片。
optionExplanations_en: Advertisers typically pull a rollup across every ad they own in one shot, and sharding by AdvertiserId means that query only has to touch one machine.
Sharding by minute doesn't match the 'view everything under my account' access pattern — clicks for one advertiser end up scattered across many shards regardless.
UserId is the clicker's dimension, unrelated to the advertiser account view, so it doesn't help this query pattern either.
Pure random placement gives up any locality, forcing an account-level query to scan every shard.

scenario: 分片键是 AdId，单个分片的硬上限是 1MB/s 或 1000 条/s。
scenario_en: The shard key is AdId, and one shard is hard-capped at 1MB/s or 1000 records/sec.
q: Nike 刚上线一条 LeBron 爆款广告，所有点击都涌向同一个分片，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens when a new Nike LeBron ad sends all clicks to one shard?
options: 流会自动重均衡，业务无影响
只有 OLAP 查询层受影响
该广告的分片被打爆：延迟涨、丢数据
其他广告的分片会先挂掉
options_en: The stream rebalances itself and nothing is affected.
Only the OLAP query layer feels it.
That ad's shard is overwhelmed: latency climbs and data can be dropped.
Other ads' shards fail first.
why: 按 AdId 分片的副作用：单个爆款广告的全部流量集中到一个分片，超过分片上限就会延迟飙升甚至丢数据——这就是热分片问题。
why_en: A viral ad funnels all its clicks into one shard, overwhelming it with higher latency and in the worst case data loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流拆分成多个可并行读写的分区，用于突破单点吞吐上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is a partition of a stream that can be read and written in parallel to exceed a single node's throughput limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分片因为流量集中而超过其吞吐上限的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot shard is a partition that receives disproportionate traffic and exceeds its throughput limit.

optionExplanations: 分片键一旦固定，key 不会自动重新分布，流不会自己重均衡。
问题源头在写入端的流分片，不只是下游 OLAP 层受影响。
这正是按 AdId 分片会踩的坑：一条爆款广告独占一个分片时，写入全砸在这一处，一旦顶穿上限，延迟先涨、最坏直接掉数据。
分片之间相互独立，一个分片过载不会传导让其他分片先挂掉。
optionExplanations_en: Once a partition key is set, keys don't automatically redistribute — the stream doesn't self-rebalance.
The problem originates at the write-side shard, not just something felt downstream in the OLAP layer.
This is the side effect of sharding by AdId: one breakout ad's entire traffic piles onto a single shard, and past its limit, latency spikes and worst case, data gets dropped.
Shards are independent — overload on one doesn't cascade into knocking out the others first.

scenario: 个别爆款广告的点击量远超单分片容量，其余广告流量正常。
scenario_en: A few hot ads exceed one shard's capacity, while normal ads do not.
q: 分区键怎么改？
q_en: How should the partition key change?
options: 所有广告统一换成随机分区键
只给热门广告的分区键加随机后缀打散
直接调大单分片容量上限
对爆款广告的点击限流丢弃
options_en: Switch every ad to a random partition key.
Only add a random suffix to the partition key of hot ads to spread them.
Just raise the per-shard capacity limit.
Rate-limit and drop clicks on viral ads.
why: 只给热广告加随机后缀（AdId:0-N），把它的流量摊到 N 个分区，普通广告保持原样，既解热点又不破坏整体聚合局部性。
why_en: Appending a random number to the partition key only for popular ads spreads a hot ad's traffic across multiple shards.
tradeoff: 只打散热点广告 vs 全量打散所有广告
whenOtherWins: 流量均匀时纯 AdId 分片最简单；全量随机分区反而会毁掉「同广告同分片」带来的聚合局部性。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    H["爆款 AdId"] --> S0["分片 AdId:0"]
    H --> S1["分片 AdId:1"]
    H --> SN["分片 AdId:N"]
    S0 --> F["Flink：写入前剥掉后缀"]
    S1 --> F
    SN --> F
    F --> O["OLAP：upsert + SUM 正确合并"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条消息进入哪个分片的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the field that determines which shard a message is routed to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给分区键追加随机后缀以打散热点流量的技巧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Salting appends a random suffix to a partition key to spread out hot traffic.

optionExplanations: 全部广告都加随机后缀会牺牲所有广告的聚合局部性，代价太大而且没必要。
只动真正过载的那条热门广告：给它的 key 加个 0 到 N 的随机尾巴，把写入拆到 N 份分区里，其余广告的分片方式原封不动。
分片吞吐上限是平台硬约束，不是可以随意调大的参数。
限流丢弃点击违反了「一条都不能丢」的要求，不是可接受的方案。
optionExplanations_en: Slapping a randomized suffix onto every single ad's key kills locality across the board — a big, unnecessary cost.
Tagging only the one overloaded ad's key with a random suffix (AdId:0-N) fans just that ad's writes out over N partitions, while every other ad's sharding stays untouched.
Per-shard throughput is a hard platform limit, not a knob you can just turn up.
Rate-limiting and dropping clicks violates the 'not a single click can be lost' requirement — not an acceptable option.

scenario: 热广告的分区键被打散成 AdId:0-N，同一广告的计数因此分散在多个分片里。
scenario_en: Hot ads get their partition key salted into AdId:0-N, so one ad's counts now live across several shards.
q: 分区键加了 AdId:0-N 后缀之后，写 OLAP 时怎么保证计数仍然正确？
q_en: After adding an AdId:0-N suffix, how do you keep OLAP counts correct?
options: 保留子键分别存储，查询时再合并求和
后缀会在 Kafka 里被自动清除掉
由浏览器端来负责合并计数
写前剥后缀，用 SUM upsert 累加
options_en: Keep the sub-keys stored separately and sum them at query time.
Kafka strips the suffix automatically.
Let the browser handle merging the counts.
Strip the suffix before writing and merge with a SUM upsert.
why: 写前剥后缀 + SUM upsert 让各子分区的部分计数在 OLAP 里正确合并；保留子键、查询时聚合也可行，但查询性能更差、不够干净。
why_en: Flink strips the random suffix before writing so upserts with sum aggregation combine the partial counts from different partitions correctly.
diagram:
graph LR
    A[adId:0] --> Sum[Query-time SUM]
    B[adId:1] --> Sum
    C[adId:N] --> Sum
    Sum --> Total[Ad total clicks]

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时如果记录已存在就更新、不存在就插入的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An upsert inserts a row if it doesn't exist yet, or updates it if it does.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对多次写入的数值做累加合并，而不是覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SUM aggregation adds up values from multiple writes instead of overwriting them.

optionExplanations: 保留子键、查询时再聚合也能凑出正确结果，但每次查询都要多做一次聚合，性能更差。
后缀是我们自己加的业务字段，Kafka 之类的流平台不会理解也不会自动处理它。
浏览器完全碰不到这条写入 OLAP 的路径，合并逻辑轮不到它做。
Flink 写入前先剥掉 AdId:0-N 后缀还原成原始 AdId，再用 SUM upsert 累加，OLAP 里直接是干净合并好的计数。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the sub-keys separate and aggregating at query time also gets a correct total, but every query then pays an extra aggregation cost.
The suffix is a field we added ourselves — a stream platform like Kafka has no idea what it means and won't strip it automatically.
The browser never touches this OLAP write path, so it has no way to do the merging.
Flink strips the AdId:0-N suffix back to the original AdId before writing, then does a SUM upsert — OLAP ends up with a clean, already-merged count.

scenario: 热广告被拆成多个子分区后，多个 Flink 任务会并发把同一 (ad_id, 分钟) 的部分计数写入 OLAP，最终计数必须等于各部分之和。
scenario_en: After a hot ad is split across sub-partitions, multiple Flink tasks concurrently write partial counts for the same (ad_id, minute) into OLAP, and the final count must equal the sum.
q: 哪种写法能保证正确合并？
q_en: Which write pattern guarantees correct merging?
options: INSERT INTO minute_agg (ad_id, minute_ts, clicks) VALUES (123, 1640000000, 40)
INSERT INTO minute_agg ... ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts) DO UPDATE SET clicks = minute_agg.clicks + EXCLUDED.clicks
INSERT INTO minute_agg ... ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts) DO UPDATE SET clicks = EXCLUDED.clicks, updated_at = now()
UPDATE minute_agg SET clicks = 40 WHERE ad_id = 123 AND minute_ts = 1640000000
why: 必须是「累加式」upsert：冲突时把新的部分计数加到已有值上。直接覆盖（SET = EXCLUDED）或裸 UPDATE 都会丢掉其他分区已写入的计数。
why_en: Only an additive upsert that sums the incoming partial count into the existing value merges concurrent writes from different partitions correctly.
tradeoff: 累加式 upsert 的正确性 vs 简单覆盖写入的低复杂度
whenOtherWins: 也可以保留 AdId:后缀 子键分行存储、查询时再 SUM 合并——写入更简单，但每次查询都变慢，通常不如写入前合并干净。
codeSample:
INSERT INTO minute_agg (ad_id, minute_ts, clicks)
VALUES (123, 1640000000, 40)
ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts)
DO UPDATE SET clicks = minute_agg.clicks + EXCLUDED.clicks;
options_en: INSERT INTO minute_agg (ad_id, minute_ts, clicks) VALUES (123, 1640000000, 40)
INSERT INTO minute_agg ... ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts) DO UPDATE SET clicks = minute_agg.clicks + EXCLUDED.clicks
INSERT INTO minute_agg ... ON CONFLICT (ad_id, minute_ts) DO UPDATE SET clicks = EXCLUDED.clicks, updated_at = now()
UPDATE minute_agg SET clicks = 40 WHERE ad_id = 123 AND minute_ts = 1640000000

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时已存在则更新、不存在则插入的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An upsert inserts a new row or updates the existing one on conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 的 upsert 语法，指定主键/唯一键冲突时的处理方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ON CONFLICT is Postgres syntax specifying what to do when an insert collides with an existing key.

termDefinitions.meaning: ON CONFLICT 子句里引用「本次尝试插入的新值」的关键字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXCLUDED refers to the row values that were proposed for insertion in an ON CONFLICT clause.

optionExplanations: 裸 INSERT 没处理主键冲突，并发写同一行会直接失败。
遇到主键冲突就把这次新算出的部分数加进已经存在的那个值，这样各分区并发写入的分量才能真正累加成总数。
覆盖式 upsert 用新值直接替换旧值，后写入会覆盖掉先写入，丢掉其他分区已经贡献的计数。
裸 UPDATE 同样是绝对值覆盖，而且行不存在时不会自动建行，会静默失败。
optionExplanations_en: A bare INSERT has no plan for the primary-key clash — two writers hitting the same row at once just error out.
On conflict, tacking the freshly arrived partial count onto whatever's already stored there is what makes concurrent partitions' pieces add up to the real total.
An overwrite-style upsert replaces the old value with the new one, so a later write wipes out whatever an earlier partition had already contributed.
A plain UPDATE also overwrites with an absolute value, and it silently does nothing if the row doesn't exist yet.

q: Kafka / Kinesis 如何天然防止单点故障丢数据？
q_en: How do Kafka or Kinesis naturally avoid losing data to a single-node failure?
options: 单副本写本地磁盘，靠客户端重试
本身不防，需要业务层自己双写
跨 broker / 跨可用区多副本复制
靠 OLAP 里的聚合结果反向恢复
options_en: Single copy on local disk, relying on client retries.
They don't protect it; the app layer must double-write.
Replication across brokers and availability zones.
Rebuild it from aggregated results in the OLAP store.
why: 两者默认就是分布式、多副本、高可用：Kafka 跨 broker、Kinesis 跨 AZ 复制，这是「不丢点击」的第一道防线。
why_en: Kafka replicates data across brokers and Kinesis across availability zones, so a single node failure does not lose click events.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 集群里负责存储和转发消息的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a Kafka cluster node that stores and serves messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商数据中心内相互隔离的物理区域，用于跨故障域容灾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An availability zone (AZ) is an isolated physical location within a cloud region, used for fault isolation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份数据在不同节点上的多份拷贝，用于容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a copy of the same data stored on a different node for fault tolerance.

scenario: 点击事件先写入 Kafka 或 Kinesis 这类分布式流平台，再由下游消费。
scenario_en: Click events first go into a distributed stream such as Kafka or Kinesis, then downstream consumers read them.
optionExplanations: 这不是两者的实际复制行为，单副本加客户端重试并不是它们默认的容错方式。
两者默认已经有内建复制机制，不需要业务层再自己造一套双写逻辑。
两个平台默认就是多副本架构：Kafka 把数据复制到不同 broker，Kinesis 复制到不同可用区，这是防止丢点击的第一道防线。
OLAP 里只有聚合后的汇总结果，反推不出丢失的原始明细事件。
optionExplanations_en: Neither actually behaves this way by default — single-replica-plus-client-retry isn't their built-in fault tolerance.
Both already replicate by default; there's no need for the business layer to reinvent a dual-write scheme on top.

Both platforms replicate out of the box — Kafka spreads copies over multiple brokers, Kinesis over multiple availability zones — and that redundancy is the first line of defense against losing a click.
OLAP only holds aggregated totals; you can't reconstruct lost raw event detail from a rollup.

scenario: 流处理器可能宕机数小时，恢复后必须把漏掉的事件全部补上，不能丢任何点击。
scenario_en: The stream processor may be down for hours, and after recovery it must catch up on every missed click.
q: 流这边要开启什么配置？
q_en: What stream configuration should you enable?
options: 消费过的数据立即删除省成本
只保留最近 1 分钟的数据
靠下游 OLAP 反查补数
开持久保留（如 7 天），消费后仍可重放
options_en: Delete consumed data immediately to save cost.
Keep only the last one minute of data.
Backfill by querying the downstream OLAP store.
Enable durable retention (e.g. 7 days) so consumed data can still be replayed.
why: 开启保留期后，流不只是管道还是短期存储：消费过的数据仍在，处理器崩溃重启后从上次的位置或时间戳重放即可补齐。
why_en: Enabling a retention period of about seven days lets a recovered stream processor replay the events it missed while it was down.
tradeoff: 更长保留期的存储成本 vs 宕机后可完整重放补数的能力
whenOtherWins: 如果原始事件已经完整归档到数据湖并能全量重算，较短的保留期也可接受，只是恢复路径更慢更绕。

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息在流里被保存的时长，过期前都可以重新读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The retention period is how long messages stay available for re-reading in the stream before expiring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从流的某个历史位置重新读取并处理数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay means re-reading and reprocessing data from an earlier point in the stream.

optionExplanations: 消费即删意味着不可回放，宕机数小时后漏掉的事件就永久丢了。
只保留最近 1 分钟的数据远撑不住数小时级别的宕机时长。
OLAP 里只有聚合结果，反查补不出丢失的原始明细事件。
把保留期拉到 7 天之后，已经被读过的数据也不会立刻消失，处理器崩了重启，就能接着上次断点或按时间戳往回补，扛住数小时的宕机。
optionExplanations_en: Delete-on-consume means no replay — anything missed during hours of downtime is gone for good.
Retaining only the last minute doesn't come close to covering hours of downtime.
OLAP only holds aggregated results; you can't back-fill lost raw detail from a rollup.
With a 7-day retention window, already-consumed data stays around, so after a crash the processor can replay from its last position and cover hours of downtime.

q: Flink 的 checkpointing 是什么？什么时候价值最大？
q_en: What is Flink checkpointing, and when is it most valuable?
options: 定期把内存状态快照到 S3，宕机后恢复
把聚合结果写入 OLAP 的机制
Kafka 的日志压缩功能
任何场景都必须开，否则必丢数据
options_en: Periodically snapshot in-memory state to S3 and recover after a crash.
A mechanism for writing aggregates into OLAP.
Kafka's log compaction feature.
It must always be on or you'll definitely lose data.
why: Checkpoint 保护的是 Flink 已算到一半的内存状态。窗口长到天/周时，从 Kafka 全量重放代价高；checkpoint 可从快照恢复，但会多一次持久化开销。
why_en: Checkpointing snapshots Flink state so a crash can resume cheaply, and it pays off most when day- or week-long windows make full replay expensive.
tradeoff: 恢复重算成本 vs checkpoint 持久化开销
diagram:
graph LR
    Flink[Flink operator state] --> CP[Checkpoint]
    CP --> Store[(Durable checkpoint store)]
    Crash[Worker crash] --> Restore[Restore state]
    Restore --> Resume[Resume from stream offset]

termDefinitions.meaning: Flink 是流处理引擎，用来持续处理事件并维护有状态计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream processing engine that continuously processes events and maintains stateful computations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理器定期把状态和进度持久化，故障后从快照继续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Checkpointing periodically persists stream state and progress so processing can resume after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算子在内存里保存的中间状态，例如窗口计数器或去重集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Operator state is intermediate data kept by a stream operator, such as window counters or dedupe sets.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon S3 是对象存储服务，常用作持久化 checkpoint 存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Amazon S3 is an object storage service often used as durable checkpoint storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: OLAP 是面向分析查询的存储或计算层，用来查询聚合或明细数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLAP is an analytics-oriented storage or compute layer used to query aggregate or detail data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 是分布式事件日志，生产者写入 topic，消费者可按 offset 重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event log where producers write to topics and consumers can replay by offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 按 key 保留较新的记录版本，用来压缩 topic 历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Log compaction is Kafka's process of keeping newer records per key to shrink topic history.

termDefinitions.meaning: offset 是消费者在事件流里读到的位置，用来从故障点继续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the position a consumer has reached in an event stream, used to resume after failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理器按时间区间归并事件的范围，比如 1 分钟、1 天或 1 周。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregation window is the time span over which a stream processor groups events, such as one minute, one day, or one week.

scenario: Flink 在内存里维护聚合状态，需要考虑进程宕机后如何恢复。
scenario_en: Flink keeps aggregation state in memory, so you need to plan how it recovers after process failure.
optionExplanations: checkpointing 定期把 Flink operator 的内存状态快照到 S3，宕机后从快照恢复，省去全量重放的代价。
把结果写进 OLAP 是 serving 层的落表动作，救不回 Flink 内存里还没算完的窗口状态。
Kafka 的日志压缩只是按 key 保留较新记录，跟 Flink 的状态快照是两码事。
小窗口且数据可重放时，强开 checkpoint 只是多花持久化开销，收益未必对得上代价。
optionExplanations_en: Checkpointing periodically snapshots Flink's in-memory operator state to S3, so a crash can recover from the snapshot instead of replaying everything.
Writing results to OLAP is a serving-layer step — it can't rescue in-flight window state still sitting in Flink's memory.
Kafka's log compaction just keeps the newest record per key — a different mechanism entirely from snapshotting Flink's state.
When windows are small and data is replayable, forcing checkpointing on just adds persistence overhead without matching benefit.

scenario: 面试官问「Flink 挂了怎么办」。我们的聚合窗口只有 1 分钟，流已开启 7 天持久保留。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what happens if Flink goes down; the aggregation window is only one minute and the stream has seven-day retention.
q: 最能体现资深判断力的回答是？
q_en: Which answer best shows senior judgment?
options: 立刻开 checkpointing，容错手段越多越好
部署三副本 Flink 热备，保状态不丢
窗口仅 1 分钟，重放重算即可，checkpoint 收益小
把聚合窗口改大，让 checkpoint 更划算
options_en: Turn on checkpointing right away; more fault tolerance is always better.
Run a three-replica hot-standby Flink so state is never lost.
The window is one minute, so replay and recompute — checkpointing buys little.
Enlarge the aggregation window so checkpointing pays off.
why: 背书式地提 checkpointing 是常见答案，但结合上下文推翻它才显资深：窗口小、流可重放，丢的状态一分钟就能重算回来。
why_en: With tiny one-minute windows and a replayable stream, you lose at most a minute of state and can simply re-aggregate, so pushing back on checkpointing shows seniority.
tradeoff: 机械套用容错最佳实践 vs 按窗口大小算清是否真的值得
whenOtherWins: 当聚合窗口很大（天/周）、内存状态昂贵时，checkpointing 就非常必要，重算一周数据不现实。

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理器定期把内存状态持久化，用于故障后恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Checkpointing periodically persists a stream processor's in-memory state so it can recover after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先启动、随时可接管的冗余副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot standby is a pre-running redundant replica that can take over immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从流的某个历史位置重新读取并处理数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay means re-reading and reprocessing data from an earlier point in the stream.

optionExplanations: 不算账就直接开 checkpoint 是常见的背书式答案，没有结合窗口大小判断实际收益。
三副本热备是为一个 1 分钟窗口的小状态问题上了过重的方案，运维和资源成本超出实际所需。
窗口只有 1 分钟、流又开了 7 天持久保留，丢的状态一分钟就能重放重算回来，checkpoint 收益远小于开销，结合上下文推翻它才显资深。
为了让 checkpoint 更划算而反过来改聚合窗口，是本末倒置，改动了题目前提而不是解决真实问题。
optionExplanations_en: Reflexively turning on checkpointing without doing the math is the common textbook answer — it skips weighing window size against actual benefit.
Three-way hot standby is overkill for a one-minute window's small amount of state — the ops and resource cost outweighs what's actually needed.

With a 1-minute window and 7-day stream retention, any lost state can be replayed and recomputed in about a minute — checkpointing's benefit is smaller than its cost, and calling that out is what shows real judgment.
Widening the window just to make checkpointing pay off is backwards — it changes the problem's premise instead of solving the real one.

scenario: 点击数据直接关联收入；流式路径可能因瞬时错误、坏代码上线、乱序事件产生细微偏差，最终数据必须正确。
scenario_en: Click data is directly tied to revenue; the streaming path can drift because of transient errors, bad deployments, or out-of-order events, but final data must be correct.
q: 加什么机制兜底？
q_en: What mechanism should you add as a safety net?
options: 每次查询都从原始点击事件全量重算
周期性对账：每天 Spark 重算纠偏
把 OLAP 换成强一致的关系型库
砍掉实时路径，只保留批处理
options_en: Recompute from all raw click events on every query.
Periodic reconciliation: a daily Spark job recomputes and corrects drift.
Swap OLAP for a strongly consistent relational database.
Drop the real-time path and keep only batch.
why: 对账 = 用慢而准的批路径校验快而近似的流路径：每天从数据湖重算一遍，对不上就查根因并回填正确值。
why_en: A periodic reconciliation job re-aggregates the raw events from the data lake with Spark and corrects any discrepancies in the OLAP data.
tradeoff: 近实时但可能有偏差 vs 每日批处理兜底换正确性
whenOtherWins: 若业务能容忍轻微误差（非计费类指标），可以省掉对账层，换取更低的系统复杂度。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用独立的批处理结果核对并修正实时结果的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reconciliation is periodically cross-checking and correcting real-time results against an independent batch computation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放原始、未加工事件数据的低成本存储，如 S3。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data lake is low-cost storage, like S3, that holds raw, unprocessed event data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式批处理计算引擎，基于 MapReduce 编程模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spark is a distributed batch-processing engine based on the MapReduce programming model.

optionExplanations: 每次查询都全量重算会把低延迟查询的要求直接打破。
对账的思路是拿准确但慢的批处理去核对快但可能有偏差的流处理：数据湖里的原始事件每天被重新算一遍，哪里对不上就顺藤摸瓜找原因，把正确值写回去。
换成强一致关系库治不了处理逻辑本身产生的误差，问题不在存储的一致性模型上。
砍掉实时路径等于重新引入分钟级延迟，放弃了近实时的需求。
optionExplanations_en: Recomputing from raw events on every query would break the low-latency requirement outright.

Reconciliation means using a slow-but-accurate batch pass to validate the fast-but-approximate stream: the raw data lake gets recomputed every day, and wherever the numbers disagree, it back-fills the correct value — speed and correctness each get their own lane.
Swapping in a strongly consistent relational store doesn't fix errors coming from the processing logic itself — the storage's consistency model isn't the issue.
Dropping the real-time path just reintroduces minute-level lag, giving up the near-real-time requirement entirely.

scenario: 对账需要一份不可变的原始点击底稿，但不能给已经打满的 Flink 任务再加负载。
scenario_en: Reconciliation needs an immutable copy of the raw clicks, but we cannot add load to an already saturated Flink job.
q: 原始点击事件怎么进 S3 数据湖最省事？
q_en: What is the easiest way to land raw click events in an S3 data lake?
options: 让 Flink 在聚合之余再写一份到 S3
从 OLAP 里定期导出再归档
让 Click Processor 双写一份到 S3
用 Kafka Connect / Firehose 原生归档
options_en: Have Flink write a second copy to S3 alongside aggregation.
Periodically export from OLAP and archive.
Have the Click Processor double-write a copy to S3.
Use Kafka Connect or Firehose to archive natively.
why: 两大流平台都有原生的 S3 归档通道（Kafka Connect Sink / Firehose），旁路落湖不占用流处理器资源，是对账数据源的标准搭法。
why_en: Kafka Connect's S3 sink and Kinesis Data Firehose archive raw events to the data lake natively without adding load to Flink.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 官方连接器，把 topic 数据持续写入 S3。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Kafka Connect S3 Sink Connector continuously streams topic data into S3.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管服务，把 Kinesis 流数据自动交付到 S3 等目的地。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis Data Firehose is a managed AWS service that automatically delivers stream data to destinations like S3.

optionExplanations: 让 Flink 在聚合之余再写一份到 S3 会占用它本该用于计算的资源和 IO。
从 OLAP 导出拿到的是聚合结果，粒度不对，对账需要的是原始明细事件。
手工在应用层双写引入了新的一致性负担，两份写入谁失败了都要处理。
两大平台都有现成的归档通路——Kafka Connect 的 S3 Sink，或者 Kinesis 这边的 Firehose——绕开主链路落湖，完全不占流处理器的资源，是标准搭法。
optionExplanations_en: Having Flink also write a copy to S3 eats into resources and I/O it should be spending on computation.
Exporting from OLAP only gets you aggregated results — wrong granularity, since reconciliation needs the raw event detail.
Manual dual-writing at the application layer creates a new consistency burden — either write can fail independently.

Both stream platforms ship a built-in path to S3 — a sink connector on the Kafka side, Firehose on the Kinesis side — a side channel that costs the stream processor nothing, the standard way to do this.

q: 补全这种「流式 + 批处理」组合架构的名字与分工：
q_en: Fill in the name and responsibilities of this streaming-plus-batch architecture:
text: 这种组合叫 {{Lambda}} 架构：{{速度层}}（Flink）提供低延迟的近实时结果，{{批处理层}}（Spark）作为真值来源，周期性地校正速度层的偏差。
why: Lambda 架构一句话：快的那条路先给答案，准的那条路定期纠错。本题的实时聚合 + 每日对账正是标准实例。
why_en: This is the Lambda architecture, where a Flink speed layer delivers low-latency results and a Spark batch layer acts as the source of truth that corrects them.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    K["Kafka / Kinesis 点击流"] --> F["速度层：Flink 实时聚合"]
    F --> O["OLAP"]
    K --> L["S3 数据湖（原始事件）"]
    L --> S["批处理层：每日 Spark 重聚合"]
    S --> R["比对差异并校正"]
    R --> O

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用实时速度层和批处理层各自输出结果、互相校正的架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Lambda architecture combines a real-time speed layer and a batch layer that cross-checks and corrects it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提供低延迟但可能不完全准确的实时结果的处理路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The speed layer is the processing path that delivers low-latency but potentially imperfect real-time results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性用完整数据重新计算、作为正确性来源的处理路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The batch layer periodically recomputes over the full dataset and serves as the source of truth.

scenario: 每天用 Spark 从数据湖重算一遍，发现实时结果和批量结果总差一点，要找出原因。
scenario_en: A nightly Spark job recomputes from the data lake and the real-time numbers are always slightly off — we need the cause.
q: 哪些因素可能让流式聚合结果出现偏差（正是对账要抓的问题）？（多选）
q_en: What can make streaming aggregation results drift and require reconciliation? (Select multiple.)
options: Flink 的瞬时处理错误
坏代码上线
OLAP 的列存格式本身会丢数据
流中的乱序事件
options_en: Transient processing errors in Flink
A bad code deployment
The OLAP store's columnar format inherently loses data
Out-of-order events in the stream
why: 瞬时处理错误、坏部署、乱序事件都可能让实时结果有细微误差；列存格式只是存储布局，不是数据丢失来源。
why_en: Transient processing errors, bad code pushes, and out-of-order events can all skew streaming results, which is exactly what reconciliation catches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 到达处理器的顺序和实际发生顺序不一致的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Out-of-order events arrive at the processor in a different order than they actually occurred.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列而非按行组织数据的存储格式，优化聚合查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Columnar storage organizes data by column rather than row, optimizing aggregate queries.

optionExplanations: 处理过程中的瞬时故障会造成局部计数偏差，正是对账要抓的问题之一。
有缺陷的代码上线可能让一整段时间的聚合结果都算错，影响范围比单条故障更大。
列存只是存储组织方式，不是造成数据丢失或算错的原因，这个说法混淆了存储布局和计算正确性。
事件到达顺序和发生顺序不一致，可能让点击落进错误的聚合窗口。
optionExplanations_en: A transient processing glitch causes a local counting discrepancy — exactly the kind of thing reconciliation is meant to catch.
A bad deploy can make an entire stretch of aggregation wrong, a wider blast radius than a single glitch.
Columnar layout is just how data is organized on disk — it has nothing to do with losing or miscounting data; this conflates storage format with compute correctness.
When arrival order doesn't match the order events actually happened, clicks can land in the wrong aggregation window.

scenario: 广告主既要几秒内看到实时点击，又要拿到能用来结算的准确数字。
scenario_en: Advertisers want click numbers within seconds and also numbers accurate enough to bill on.
q: 「正确性 vs 低延迟」这对天然矛盾，本系统靠什么方式平衡？
q_en: How does this system balance correctness against low latency?
options: 两条路径互补：速度层保快、批层对账保准
只能二选一，放弃其中之一
直接把正确性要求降级
无限加机器就能同时满足
options_en: Two complementary paths: the speed layer stays fast, the batch layer reconciles for accuracy.
You must pick one and give up the other.
Just downgrade the accuracy requirement.
Adding unlimited machines satisfies both at once.
why: 点击数据关乎收入，既要快也要准。速度层先给近似的实时答案，批层每天用完整数据重算并纠偏，两者合起来就是平衡。
why_en: The system balances correctness against latency by pairing a fast streaming path with a periodic batch path that serves as the source of truth.
tradeoff: 速度层的低延迟近似结果 vs 批处理层的高延迟高正确性结果

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用实时速度层和批处理层各自输出结果、互相校正的架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Lambda architecture combines a real-time speed layer and a batch layer that cross-checks and corrects it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提供低延迟但可能不完全准确的实时结果的处理路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The speed layer is the processing path that delivers low-latency but potentially imperfect real-time results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性用完整数据重新计算、作为正确性来源的处理路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The batch layer periodically recomputes over the full dataset and serves as the source of truth.

optionExplanations: 先由速度层顶上去，给一个大概靠谱的实时数字；批处理层每天拿全量数据重新算一遍纠错；两条腿走路，快和准都不用舍。
点击数据既关乎收入又要求近实时，放弃其中一个都不满足需求，不是非此即彼的选择。
计费相关指标通常不接受降级，直接放低正确性要求违反了业务约束。
加机器能提升吞吐，但治不了处理逻辑本身产生的误差，扩容解决不了正确性问题。
optionExplanations_en: The speed layer gives a fast approximate answer now, while the batch layer recomputes from complete data daily and corrects it — the two paths complement each other.
Clicks both drive revenue and need near-real-time visibility — dropping either fails the requirements; it isn't really an either/or choice.
Billing-adjacent metrics generally can't tolerate a lowered accuracy bar — downgrading correctness violates the business constraint.
More machines raise throughput, but they don't fix errors coming from the processing logic itself — scaling out doesn't buy correctness.

scenario: 同一次展示里用户手抖连点三下只该计费一次；同一广告再营销重新展示则该重新计费。
scenario_en: Three rage-clicks on one impression should bill once, but a re-marketed impression of the same ad should bill again.
q: 「幂等点击跟踪」在本题的准确含义是？
q_en: What does idempotent click tracking mean in this problem?
options: 同一个用户对任何广告永远只算一次点击
广告只能被点击一次
同一广告实例上的重复点击只算一次
点击可以重复计数，但要打上标记
options_en: The same user's click on any ad is only ever counted once.
An ad can only be clicked one time, period.
A duplicate click on the same ad instance only counts once.
Clicks can be double-counted, as long as duplicates are flagged.
why: 幂等的粒度是「广告实例」：同一次展示上点多少次都只算一次；不同展示（再营销）各自独立计数。
why_en: Idempotency is scoped to one ad impression — click it many times and it counts once; a different impression counts separately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作无论重复执行多少次，效果都等同于执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating an operation any number of times has the same effect as doing it once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告被展示给用户的一次具体呈现，同一广告可以产生多个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one concrete instance of an ad being shown; the same ad can generate many impressions.

optionExplanations: 这个粒度太粗，会把同一用户在不同展示（再营销）上的合法重复点击也计成重复。
广告是被无数用户共享点击的资源，不存在「只能被点击一次」这种限制。
这题要的幂等粒度锁在单次展示上：不管在同一次曝光里点了几下，都只记一次；换一次新的展示，就是全新独立的计数。
允许重复计数只是打标记，并没有真正实现幂等——幂等要求重复点击不改变最终计数结果。
optionExplanations_en: This granularity is too coarse — it would also flag a user's legitimate repeat clicks on separate ad displays (retargeting) as duplicates.
An ad is a resource clicked by countless users — there's no such thing as being 'clicked only once'.

The unit that matters here is a single ad showing: click it five times, it's still one count; a fresh showing of the same ad starts its own independent count — that blocks real duplicates without punishing retargeting.
Letting duplicates through with a flag isn't real idempotency — idempotent means a repeat click can't change the final count.

scenario: 大量点击来自未登录用户，同一用户还会在信息流和侧栏多次看到同一条广告。
scenario_en: Many clicks come from logged-out users, and the same user sees the same ad again in the feed and the sidebar.
q: 「强制登录 + 按 userId+adId 去重」这个朴素方案的两大问题是？
q_en: What are the two main problems with forcing login and deduping by userId plus adId?
options: JWT 解析开销太大，拖慢点击路径
登录假设不成立，且去重粒度错在按广告而非按展示实例
Redis 容量存不下海量 userId 索引
点击事件里压根拿不到 adId 字段
options_en: JWT parsing overhead is too high and slows down the click path.
The login assumption doesn't hold, and the dedup granularity is wrong — it should be per impression, not per ad.
Redis can't hold the volume of userId indexes at this scale.
The click event doesn't actually carry an adId field.
why: 登录是产品层面的假设，未必满足；更致命的是它把去重粒度定错了——应该是「每用户每广告实例一次」而不是「每用户每广告一次」。
why_en: Requiring login may not hold, and deduping by user and ad ID wrongly merges legitimate repeat clicks from retargeting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告主故意在一段时间内向同一用户重复展示同一广告，是正常且常见的投放策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retargeting is when an advertiser deliberately re-shows the same ad to the same user multiple times, a normal advertising strategy.

optionExplanations: JWT 校验是微秒级操作，性能从来不是这个朴素方案被否决的原因。
登录是产品层面的假设未必成立，更致命的是把去重粒度定成「每用户每广告」而不是「每用户每广告实例」，会漏掉再营销场景下的合法重复点击。
userId 只有几十字节，容量从不是这里的瓶颈。
adId 本就是点击事件自带的字段，取数从来不是障碍。
optionExplanations_en: JWT verification is a microsecond-level operation — performance was never why this naive approach gets rejected.
The login assumption may not hold, and worse, it sets the de-dup granularity to 'per user per ad' instead of 'per user per ad instance,' missing legitimate repeat clicks under retargeting.
A userId is only a few dozen bytes — capacity was never the bottleneck here.
adId is already a field on the click event itself — fetching it was never the obstacle.

scenario: 同一用户在信息流和侧栏各看到同一条广告，要判断这算一次还是两次计费机会。
scenario_en: The same user sees the same ad in the feed and in the sidebar — is that one billable opportunity or two?
q: 什么是一次 impression（曝光）？
q_en: What is an impression?
options: 用户点击广告发生的那一次动作
广告主期待的转化行为发生一次
广告素材第一次被创建出来的时刻
广告被展示一次，换位置就是新曝光
options_en: The single moment a user clicks the ad.
The moment the advertiser's desired conversion happens.
The moment the ad creative is first created.
The ad is shown once; a new placement is a new impression.
why: 曝光按「展示」计数而不是按「广告」计数：同一用户在不同位置多次看到同一广告，就是多次曝光。这正是去重键的正确粒度。
why_en: An impression counts each time an ad is fetched and displayed, so the same ad shown in multiple placements yields multiple impressions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告被展示给用户的一次具体呈现，同一广告可以产生多个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one concrete instance of an ad being shown; the same ad can generate many impressions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点击广告后完成了广告主期望的后续行为，例如下单或注册。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conversion is when a user completes the advertiser's desired action after clicking, such as a purchase or signup.

optionExplanations: 点击是曝光之后的下游行为，两者是分子分母关系，不能画等号。
转化跟踪是题目明确排除的范围，跟曝光定义无关。
一条广告创建后能展示成千上万次，创建只发生一次，跟曝光计数完全是两件事。
曝光的计数单位是每一次展示：同一个人如果在页面不同位置各撞见一次同一条广告，那就是两次独立曝光——这也是去重键该对齐的颗粒度。
optionExplanations_en: A click is a downstream action after an impression — the two are numerator and denominator, not the same thing.
Conversion tracking is explicitly out of scope for this problem and unrelated to how an impression is defined.
An ad is created exactly once but can then be shown thousands of times — creating it and tallying how often it's seen are two completely different events.

Each individual display is its own impression: if the same user sees the same ad in a different spot on the page, that's a second, separate impression — and that's the granularity the de-dup key has to match.

scenario: 要求「每个用户每次看到的广告实例只计一次点击」，且不能强制用户登录。
scenario_en: Each ad instance shown to a user should count at most one click, and users cannot be forced to log in.
q: 去重键应该用什么？
q_en: What should the dedupe key be?
options: 登录用户的 userId 拼接 adId 作为去重键
客户端 IP 地址加 User-Agent 指纹
系统为每次广告展示单独生成的唯一 impression ID
点击发生的时间戳精确到秒级
options_en: The logged-in userId concatenated with the adId.
The client's IP address plus its User-Agent fingerprint.
The unique impression ID the system mints separately for every ad instance shown.
The click's timestamp, precise to the second.
why: impression ID 的粒度正好是「广告实例」：随广告下发到浏览器，点击时带回来作为幂等键，既不依赖登录，也兼容再营销。
why_en: A unique impression ID minted per ad instance serves as the idempotency key, sent to the browser with the ad and returned with the click.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品保证全员登录、且不存在再营销这类重复展示语义，userId+adId 去重实现更简单。
tradeoff: 依赖登录识别用户 vs 用免登录的展示级唯一标识去重

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告展示服务为每次广告曝光生成的唯一标识符，用作去重的幂等键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression ID is a unique identifier minted for each ad impression, used as the idempotency key for deduplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用网络地址和浏览器标识拼出的模糊用户特征，不是稳定唯一的标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP plus User-Agent fingerprinting combines network address and browser string into a fuzzy signal, not a stable unique ID.

optionExplanations: 需要登录识别用户，违反「不能强制登录」的约束，粒度也定在广告而非展示实例，会误伤再营销。
IP 和 User-Agent 拼出来的指纹既不唯一也不稳定，同一 WiFi 下多用户共享 IP，换网络指纹也会变。
系统在每次广告展示时都会单独生成一个 impression ID，随广告下发到浏览器，天然满足免登录和展示级去重粒度两条约束。
秒级时间戳不具备唯一性，热门广告下同一秒内的不同点击会被误判成重复。
optionExplanations_en: This needs a logged-in user, violating the 'can't require login' constraint, and its granularity is per-ad rather than per-impression, misfiring on retargeting.
An IP-plus-User-Agent fingerprint is neither unique nor stable — users sharing WiFi share an IP, and the fingerprint shifts when the network changes.
The system mints a brand-new impression ID for every display and ships it down to the client alongside the ad — that alone satisfies both no-login and impression-level de-dup granularity.
A second-level timestamp isn't unique — under a popular ad, distinct clicks in the same second get misjudged as duplicates.

q: 为什么去重不能放在 Flink 的聚合逻辑里做？
q_en: Why shouldn't deduplication live inside Flink aggregation?
options: 重复点击可能落在分钟边界两侧，互相看不见
Flink 没有可用的状态存储
Kafka 不允许消费前修改数据
Flink 的窗口内存放不下去重集合
options_en: Duplicate clicks can land on either side of a minute boundary and never see each other.
Flink has no usable state storage.
Kafka doesn't allow modifying data before it's consumed.
Flink's window memory can't hold the dedup set.
why: 窗口内去重挡不住跨窗口的重复：同一 impression 的两次点击分别落在 12:00:59 和 12:01:01 就会各计一次。去重必须前置到入流之前。
why_en: Deduplication must happen before the stream because duplicates landing on opposite sides of a window boundary would otherwise be counted twice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种流处理框架，按事件时间做窗口聚合，并提供状态管理和容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework that performs windowed aggregation on event time with built-in state management and fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，用来缓冲和持久化事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging log used to buffer and durably store event streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理里按固定时间切分数据并分别计算指标的时间段，例如每分钟一个窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregation window is a fixed time slice, like one minute, over which a stream processor computes metrics.

scenario: 点击已经进入 Flink，按分钟窗口做实时聚合后写入 OLAP。
scenario_en: The click has already entered Flink, which aggregates by minute windows and writes to OLAP.
optionExplanations: 同一次广告展示对应的两次点击完全可能一个落在 12:00:58、另一个落在 12:01:02，跨过了分钟边界，窗口内去重根本看不到彼此，两次都会各算一次。
状态管理正是 Flink 的核心能力之一，它并不缺少维护中间状态的能力。
问题不在 Kafka 能不能在消费前改数据，瓶颈是去重发生的时机太晚。
就算内存无限大，跨窗口边界的重复依旧存在，问题不是内存容量。
optionExplanations_en: Two clicks on the same impression can land on opposite sides of a minute boundary — say 12:00:58 and 12:01:02 — and dedup inside a single window simply can't see across that line, so both get counted.
State management is one of Flink's core capabilities; it isn't missing the ability to hold intermediate state.
The issue isn't whether Kafka lets you mutate data before consumption — the real bottleneck is de-duplication happening too late.
Even with unlimited memory, cross-window duplicates would still slip through — capacity was never the actual constraint.

scenario: 点击到达 Click Processor 时要用 impression ID 判重：重复的丢弃，新的进流。
scenario_en: When a click reaches the Click Processor, it uses impression ID to dedupe: duplicates are dropped and new clicks enter the stream.
q: 正确的处理流程是？
q_en: What is the correct processing flow?
options: 先写缓存占位，再写流
查缓存命中即丢弃；未命中先写流再登记缓存
全部直接入流，靠 Flink 窗口内去重
写 OLAP 时按主键去重
options_en: Write a cache placeholder first, then write to the stream.
Check the cache: a hit means drop it; a miss means write to the stream first, then register the ID.
Send everything straight into the stream and rely on Flink's window-level dedup.
Dedup by primary key when writing to the OLAP table.
why: 缓存是「见过的 impression ID」集合：命中即重复。新点击必须先落流再登记缓存，保证任何失败模式下点击本身不丢。
why_en: On each click we check the cache for the impression ID, drop it if present, and otherwise write to the stream first and then record the ID in the cache.
whenOtherWins: 若业务能容忍跨窗口的少量重复且没有对账需求，Flink 窗口内去重能挡住部分重复，实现更简单但不完整。
tradeoff: 先写流保事件 vs 先写缓存保不重复
diagram:
graph LR
    Click[Click with impressionId] --> Seen{Seen in dedup cache?}
    Seen -->|yes| Drop[Drop duplicate]
    Seen -->|no| Stream[Write event to stream]
    Stream --> Mark[Mark impression seen]
    Mark --> Redirect[Return redirect]

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析查询优化的列式数据库，擅长聚合但不擅长高频单条写入去重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An OLAP database is a columnar store optimized for analytical aggregation, not for high-frequency per-row dedup writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录「已经见过的 impression ID」的缓存集合，命中即判定为重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The dedup cache stores impression IDs already seen; a hit means the click is a duplicate.

optionExplanations: 顺序颠倒：先标记缓存再写流，一旦写流失败，这条点击就永久丢了，拿丢事件的风险换不来任何好处。
缓存命中即判重丢弃；未命中先落流再登记缓存，任一步失败最多造成可被对账修正的重复，但不会丢事件。
只靠 Flink 窗口内去重挡不住跨窗口的重复（见前一张卡），幂等要求覆盖不全。
点击早被聚合成汇总行，写 OLAP 阶段已经没有单条点击可去重，时机太晚。
optionExplanations_en: This has the order backwards — marking the cache before writing to the stream means a stream-write failure loses the click permanently, trading a real risk for no real benefit.
A cache hit means discard as duplicate; a miss writes to the stream first, then registers in the cache — either step failing produces at most a fixable duplicate, never a lost event.
Relying only on Flink's in-window dedup misses duplicates that straddle a window boundary (see the earlier card) — idempotency coverage is incomplete.
By the time data reaches OLAP it's already aggregated into rollups — there's no individual click left to dedup, far too late.

scenario: 点击处理服务要写 Kafka 和 Redis 去重缓存两步，中间可能崩；漏记点击等于漏收钱。
scenario_en: The click processor writes to Kafka and to the Redis dedup cache and can crash in between — a lost click is lost revenue.
q: 去重流程里为什么必须「先写流、再写缓存」而不是反过来？
q_en: Why must the dedupe flow write to the stream before writing to the cache?
options: 因为缓存的写入延迟明显更高
因为 Kafka 要求先收到事件
两个顺序的效果完全一样
缓存失败只是重复，入流失败点击永久丢失
options_en: Because the cache write is noticeably slower.
Because Kafka requires receiving the event first.
Both orderings end up identical.
A cache failure only risks a duplicate; a stream failure loses the click forever.
why: 这是不对称的失败权衡：多计一次能被每日对账修正，漏计一次却无处找回。所以宁可先保住事件、缓存登记放后面。
why_en: Writing the stream first means a cache failure only risks a fixable duplicate, while the reverse order could lose a click for good.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期用离线批处理重新计算结果，与线上结果比对纠错的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reconciliation is a periodic batch job that recomputes results offline and corrects discrepancies against the live pipeline.

optionExplanations: 两者写入延迟其实都是毫秒级，延迟大小不是决定顺序的依据。
这是我们自己的容错设计选择，不是 Kafka 协议本身强制要求的顺序。
两种顺序的失败后果完全不同：先写缓存失败会让事件永久丢失，说效果一样忽视了这点。
这是不对称的失败权衡：缓存登记失败只造成可被每日对账修正的重复，入流失败却让点击永久找不回，所以宁可先保住事件。
optionExplanations_en: Both writes are actually millisecond-scale — latency size isn't what decides the ordering here.
This is our own fault-tolerance design choice, not something Kafka's protocol requires.
The failure consequences of the two orderings are completely different: failing cache-first loses the event permanently — claiming they're the same ignores that.

It's an asymmetric tradeoff: a failed cache registration only causes a duplicate that daily reconciliation can fix, while a failed stream write loses the click for good — so the event gets saved first.

scenario: impression ID 随点击 URL 暴露在客户端，攻击者能任意构造请求刷广告主预算。
scenario_en: The impression ID rides in the click URL on the client, so an attacker can craft requests and burn the advertiser's budget.
q: 只靠「唯一 impression ID 去重」会被怎么攻击？怎么防？
q_en: How can unique impression IDs still be attacked, and how do you defend against it?
options: 伪造全新唯一 ID 冒充点击；用签名绑定 adId
反复重放同一个已用过的 ID；把 ID 加长
攻击者直接清空我们的去重缓存；防法加装防火墙
唯一性天然防伪造，这套设计无法被攻击
options_en: Forge brand-new unique IDs; the fix is signing the ID together with the adId.
Replay one already-used ID; the "fix" is making IDs longer.
An attacker wipes out our dedup cache directly; the fix is adding a firewall.
Uniqueness alone naturally prevents forgery — this design can't be attacked.
why: 去重只挡「重复」，挡不住「伪造的新 ID」。签名让只有我们下发的 ID 才验得过，伪造的 ID 直接被拒。
why_en: An attacker could flood the system with fabricated unique impression IDs, so we sign each ID with an HMAC and verify the signature on every click.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用密钥生成消息摘要的对称签名算法，用来验证数据完整性和来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HMAC is a symmetric keyed hash algorithm used to verify a message's integrity and origin.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用同一把密钥重新计算签名并比对，判断数据是否被篡改或伪造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Signature verification recomputes the signature with the shared key and compares it to detect tampering or forgery.

optionExplanations: 去重只挡「重复」，挡不住「凭空伪造的新 ID」；用密钥签名 ID 和 adId，伪造的 ID 验签阶段就直接被拒。
重放同一个 ID 本就会被去重缓存拦住，不是真正的缺口，加长 ID 也防不住伪造全新 ID 这种攻击。
直接攻破缓存基础设施是另一个层面的问题，防火墙防不住来自合法客户端的应用层伪造请求。
唯一只保证不重复，不等于防伪造，这个假设本身不成立。
optionExplanations_en: De-duplication only blocks repeats, not a brand-new forged ID — signing the ID together with the adId means a forged ID simply fails verification.
Replaying the same ID is already caught by the dedup cache, so that's not the real gap, and lengthening the ID doesn't stop someone forging an entirely new one.
Breaching the cache infrastructure directly is a different threat layer — a firewall doesn't stop application-layer forgery from a legitimate client.
Uniqueness only guarantees no duplicates, not forgery resistance — that assumption doesn't hold.

scenario: 签名只覆盖 impression ID 时，攻击者手里已经有一批我们签发过的合法签名。
scenario_en: If the signature covers only the impression ID, an attacker already holds a batch of legitimately signed ones.
q: HMAC 签名时为什么要把 adId 一起签进去？
q_en: Why include adId in the HMAC signature?
options: 为了让签名字符串更难被猜出规律
为了方便按 adId 做流分片
防止把一条广告的合法签名重放到另一条广告上
为了压缩点击事件的传输体积
options_en: To make the signature string harder to guess the pattern of.
To make sharding the stream by adId easier.
To stop a valid signature from one ad being replayed onto another ad.
To compress the size of the click event payload.
why: 只签 ID 本身挡不住「换广告重放」：拿到一批合法签名后打到别的广告上。把 adId 绑进签名，验签即校验两者匹配。
why_en: Signing the ad ID together with the impression ID prevents attackers from harvesting valid signed IDs and replaying them against different ads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 攻击者截获一份合法的凭证或签名，原样在别处重新使用来伪装合法请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replay attack reuses a captured valid credential or signature elsewhere to impersonate a legitimate request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用密钥生成消息摘要的对称签名算法，用来验证数据完整性和来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HMAC is a symmetric keyed hash algorithm used to verify a message's integrity and origin.

optionExplanations: 签名安全性靠密钥强度和算法本身，不靠签进去的内容长度。
分片键是流处理层的路由决策，跟签名内容要不要包含 adId 是两回事。
只签 impression ID 本身，挡不住把一条广告的合法签名整个搬到另一条广告上重放；让签名同时覆盖 adId，验证时就能揪出这种不匹配。
签进 adId 会让载荷变大，跟压缩传输体积的方向正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Signature security comes from key strength and the algorithm itself, not from how much content gets signed.
Sharding key is a routing decision made at the stream layer, unrelated to whether adId is folded into the signature.

Signing just that one identifier can't stop someone lifting a valid signature off one ad and replaying it on another — folding the adId into what gets signed is what makes that mismatch fail verification.
Adding the adId makes the payload bigger, the opposite direction from compressing transfer size.

q: 在点击路径上做 HMAC 验签，开销是什么量级？
q_en: What is the latency cost of HMAC verification on the click path?
options: 毫秒级，必须异步化
秒级，需要专用硬件
取决于 RSA 密钥长度
微秒级——一次哈希计算，延迟可忽略
options_en: Millisecond-scale, so it has to be done asynchronously.
Second-scale, so it needs dedicated hardware.
It depends on the RSA key length.
Microsecond-scale — one hash computation, negligible latency.
optionExplanations: 毫秒级是把 HMAC 想成远程调用或非对称签名了，单次本地哈希不会这么慢。
秒级和专用硬件是过度担心，普通点击服务就能同步完成验签。
RSA 密钥长度影响的是非对称签名，不是 HMAC 这种共享密钥哈希。
微秒级符合本题：验签在入流前同步做，不会成为点击路径瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Millisecond-scale confuses HMAC with a remote call or asymmetric signature; a local keyed hash is much cheaper.
Second-scale latency and dedicated hardware are overkill; a normal click service can verify this inline.
RSA key length matters for asymmetric signatures, not for HMAC's shared-key hash.
Microsecond-scale is the right mental model here: verify before enqueueing without making it the bottleneck.
why: HMAC 只是对称哈希运算，微秒级完成，比 RSA 这类非对称签名快几个数量级——点击路径可以同步验签，不用异步化或做批处理缓冲。
why_en: HMAC verification is a microsecond-scale hash, cheap enough to run synchronously right in the click path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用密钥生成消息摘要的对称签名算法，用来验证数据完整性和来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HMAC is a symmetric keyed hash algorithm used to verify a message's integrity and origin.

termDefinitions.meaning: 使用公钥私钥对的加密算法，验证运算比对称哈希慢得多，常见于数字签名场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RSA is an asymmetric public/private key algorithm; its signature verification is much slower than a symmetric hash like HMAC.

scenario: 点击到达 Click Processor 后要先验签，验签通过才判断是否重复。
scenario_en: After a click reaches the Click Processor, it verifies the signature before checking whether the click is a duplicate.

scenario: 每天约 1 亿次点击，每个 impression ID 16 字节，去重缓存一天的数据量约 1.6GB。
scenario_en: The system sees about 100 million clicks per day; each impression ID is 16 bytes, so one day of dedupe-cache entries is about 1.6 GB.
q: 这个数据量对去重缓存的容量规划意味着什么？
q_en: What does this data size imply for dedupe-cache capacity planning?
options: 数据量已经逼近单机内存上限，必须提前分片
单机内存就装得下，Cluster 扩容是稳妥而非刚需
这个量级建议改用磁盘型 KV 存储
数据量太小不需要任何持久化措施
options_en: The volume is already near a single machine's memory limit, so we must pre-shard.
It fits easily in one machine's memory — clustering is about safety margin, not a capacity necessity.
At this scale we should switch to a disk-based KV store.
The volume is so small that no persistence is needed at all.
why: 1.6GB 单机内存轻松放下，去重缓存的容量从来不是这里的瓶颈；上 Redis Cluster 和持久化是为了可用性和防丢数据，不是为了扩容量。
why_en: One point six gigabytes fits easily in one machine's memory, so clustering here is about durability and failover, not capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的分布式集群模式，把数据按哈希槽分散到多个节点，用来提升容量和吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster is Redis's distributed mode that shards data across nodes by hash slot to scale capacity and throughput.

optionExplanations: 1.6GB 远没有逼近单机内存的常见上限，提前分片不是这个量级逼出来的。
1.6GB 这个体量随便一台机器的内存都装得下，容量从来没真正逼近过瓶颈；上 Cluster 买的是高可用和防丢数据的保险，不是为了腾容量。
磁盘型 KV 换来的是持久化，不是容量：内存已经装得下，没必要为容量原因换存储介质。
数据量小不等于不需要持久化：宕机重启后去重状态一样会丢，持久化解决的是可用性而不是容量。
optionExplanations_en: 1.6GB is nowhere near a typical single-machine memory limit — this size doesn't force early sharding.

1.6GB is a small enough number that a single box's RAM swallows it whole — capacity was never the constraint; clustering here buys availability and durability insurance, not headroom you actually need.
A disk-backed KV store buys you durability rather than more room — memory already holds this fine, so there's no capacity-driven reason to switch storage medium.
Small data volume doesn't mean no durability is needed — a restart still wipes de-dup state without it; persistence is about availability, not size.

scenario: 去重缓存丢一个键就会放进一次重复计费；峰值 1 万点击/秒，缓存节点会挂会重启。
scenario_en: One lost key in the dedup cache means one double-billed click, at 10k clicks/sec, with nodes that crash and restart.
q: 去重缓存的扩展与容灾应该怎么做？（多选）
q_en: How should the dedupe cache scale and recover from failures? (Select multiple.)
options: 用 Redis Cluster 做分布式扩容
为了写入性能关闭持久化，接受丢数据
挂副本：主节点挂掉后由副本接管
开启 Redis 持久化（RDB 或 AOF），缓存重启后数据不丢
options_en: Scale the dedup cache out using Redis Cluster.
Turn off persistence for write performance and accept data loss.
Add a replica so it takes over if the primary node dies.
Enable Redis persistence (RDB or AOF) so cache data survives a restart.
why: 去重缓存一旦丢数据就会放进重复点击，所以要 Cluster 扩容、副本接管、RDB/AOF 持久化三管齐下；关持久化与目标背道而驰。
why_en: Scale the dedup cache with Redis Cluster, add a replica for failover, and enable RDB or AOF persistence so the cached IDs survive a restart.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的分布式集群模式，把数据按哈希槽分散到多个节点，用来提升容量和吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster is Redis's distributed mode that shards data across nodes by hash slot to scale capacity and throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的两种持久化机制：RDB 定期打快照，AOF 记录每条写命令，用于重启后恢复数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDB and AOF are Redis's two persistence mechanisms — periodic snapshots versus a write-command log — used to restore data after a restart.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点故障时由同步的副本节点接管服务，避免单点故障造成服务中断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a synced standby node that takes over when the primary fails, avoiding a single point of failure.

optionExplanations: Cluster 分布式扩容挡住未来流量增长和单机容量上限带来的风险。
关闭持久化换写入速度背离了去重缓存本身的职责——它存在的目的就是防重复，关掉持久化等于放弃这个目标。
挂副本让主节点故障时由副本接管，挡住单点故障造成的服务中断。
开启 RDB/AOF 让缓存重启后已见过的 ID 集合还在，挡住重启导致的去重状态丢失、老点击被误判为新点击的风险。
optionExplanations_en: Redis Cluster scaling out heads off the risk of hitting single-node capacity limits as traffic grows.
Turning off persistence for write speed undercuts the whole point of a dedup cache — it exists to prevent duplicates, so dropping persistence abandons that goal.
A replica lets a standby take over when the primary fails, closing off the single-point-of-failure risk.
RDB/AOF persistence keeps the set of already-seen IDs intact across a restart, closing off the risk of old clicks getting miscounted as new.

q: 把幂等点击跟踪的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full idempotent click-tracking flow in order:
steps: Click Processor 验证 impression ID 的签名
Ad Placement Service 为每次广告展示生成唯一的 impression ID
未命中：先把点击写入流，再把 impression ID 加进缓存
用户点击广告，浏览器把签名的 impression ID 随点击数据一起发回
用密钥对 impression ID（连同 adId）做 HMAC 签名，随广告一起下发到浏览器
查询缓存：命中说明是重复点击，直接丢弃
why: 生成 ID → 签名下发 → 点击带回 → 验签 → 查重 → 先写流再登记缓存，这条链同时解决了去重、防伪造、防丢三件事。
why_en: This flow mints, signs, and verifies the impression ID, writing to the stream before caching it — solving dedup, forgery, and loss together.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    G["生成 impression ID"] --> S["HMAC 签名后随广告下发"]
    S --> C["点击时浏览器带回 ID"]
    C --> V["验签"]
    V --> D{"缓存里已存在？"}
    D -->|是| X["重复，丢弃"]
    D -->|否| W["先写流，再写缓存"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告展示服务为每次广告曝光生成的唯一标识符，用作去重的幂等键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression ID is a unique identifier minted for each ad impression, used as the idempotency key for deduplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用密钥生成消息摘要的对称签名算法，用来验证数据完整性和来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HMAC is a symmetric keyed hash algorithm used to verify a message's integrity and origin.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作无论重复执行多少次，效果都等同于执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating an operation any number of times has the same effect as doing it once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 攻击者截获一份合法的凭证或签名，原样在别处重新使用来伪装合法请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replay attack reuses a captured valid credential or signature elsewhere to impersonate a legitimate request.

scenario: 广告主打开报表要求亚秒级返回，而底层是每天几十亿条原始点击。
scenario_en: The advertiser dashboard must answer in under a second on top of billions of raw clicks per day.
q: 「广告主查询要低延迟」这条需求主要靠什么已经解决了？
q_en: What already solves the advertiser low-latency query requirement?
options: 写入路径上已经预聚合好，查询只读汇总行
OLAP 表额外加装了全文检索索引
查询结果被前端客户端缓存住了
系统限制了广告主的查询频率
options_en: Data was already pre-aggregated, synchronously or in batch, on the write path, so queries just read summary rows.
A full-text search index was added on top of the OLAP table.
Query results get cached on the client side.
The system throttles how often advertisers can query.
why: 昂贵的聚合在数据进库前就完成了（Flink 实时或 Spark 批量），查询天然是读汇总，低延迟基本是白送的。
why_en: Low-latency queries come almost for free because the expensive aggregation already happened upstream before the data landed in the OLAP store.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析查询优化的列式数据库，擅长聚合但不擅长高频单条写入去重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An OLAP database is a columnar store optimized for analytical aggregation, not for high-frequency per-row dedup writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 针对文本内容做分词和倒排索引，用于加速关键词搜索，不是用来加速聚合统计的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full-text index tokenizes text for fast keyword search; it does not speed up aggregate queries.

optionExplanations: 真正费算力的聚合工作，在数据落库之前就被 Flink 的实时管道或 Spark 的批处理跑完了，查询这边只是读现成汇总，低延迟几乎是白捡的。
全文检索索引加速的是关键词匹配，对数值型聚合查询没有帮助。
客户端缓存只能加速同一广告主重复发起的相同查询，覆盖不了低延迟这条整体需求。
限流管的是保护系统吞吐，不会让单次查询本身变快。
optionExplanations_en: All the costly number-crunching is done upstream — by Flink in real time or Spark in batch — before anything reaches the store, so a query just reads a rollup that's already sitting there, and speed comes along for free.
A full-text index speeds up keyword matching, which doesn't help a numeric aggregation query.
Client-side caching only speeds up the same advertiser repeating the same query — it can't cover the low-latency requirement broadly.
Rate limiting protects overall system throughput; it doesn't make any single query run faster.

scenario: 广告主查「过去一年」的趋势曲线，即使读的是分钟级汇总表也要扫几十万行，仍然慢。
scenario_en: An advertiser queries a one-year trend line; even minute-level rollups require scanning hundreds of thousands of rows and are still slow.
q: 怎么优化这类大时间跨度查询？
q_en: How would you optimize this kind of long-range query?
options: 提示广告主耐心等待结果
直接拒绝跨度超过一周的查询
夜间批处理出天/周汇总表，按需下钻
每次现算，再把结果缓存一分钟
options_en: Tell advertisers to be patient.
Reject any query spanning more than a week.
A nightly batch builds daily and weekly rollups, drilling down on demand.
Compute it fresh each time and cache for a minute.
why: 在 OLAP 内部再做一层更粗粒度的预聚合（rollup 表），大跨度查询读天/周级行，行数骤减、速度回升，需要细节再下钻。
why_en: A nightly job pre-aggregates the data into daily or weekly rollup tables so long-range queries read far fewer rows and drill down only when needed.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询集中在近期的分钟级数据，基础分钟表已经够快，维护额外汇总表反而是白花的存储和运维成本。
tradeoff: 多存一份粗粒度汇总换查询提速 vs 只维护分钟级明细省存储

termDefinitions.meaning: 在已有明细表基础上，按更粗粒度（天/周）再聚合出的表，用来加速大范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup table re-aggregates existing detail data at a coarser grain like day or week to speed up wide-range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表自动触发的批处理作业，例如每天凌晨跑一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cron job is a batch task that runs automatically on a fixed schedule, such as nightly.

optionExplanations: 提示耐心等待是在回避问题，没有减少任何实际要扫描的行数。
直接拒绝长跨度查询砍掉了「查一年趋势」这个真实需求，是功能倒退而不是优化。
夜间批处理再聚合出天/周级汇总表，大跨度查询改读少量行，需要细节再下钻回分钟级，直接针对「扫描行数太多」这个根因。
现算再缓存一分钟只帮到短时间内的重复查询，第一次查询依旧要全量扫描，没有减少底层要扫的行数。
optionExplanations_en: Asking the advertiser to wait sidesteps the problem — it doesn't reduce how many rows actually get scanned.
Flatly refusing queries that span a long time window kills the real 'view a year's trend' requirement — that's a regression, not an optimization.

A nightly batch job re-aggregates into day/week rollups, so a wide-range query only has to touch a small fraction of the rows and can drill back down to minute-level when needed — this directly attacks the row-scan problem at its root.
Computing on demand and caching for a minute only helps a repeated query within that window — the first hit still does a full scan, so the underlying row count never shrinks.

scenario: OLAP 里已有分钟级明细，广告主最常查最近 30 天的日汇总，存储预算并不紧张。
scenario_en: OLAP already holds minute-level rows, advertisers mostly query 30-day daily rollups, and storage budget is not the constraint.
q: OLAP 内预聚合（rollup 汇总表）的本质权衡是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff of OLAP rollup tables?
options: 用一致性换取可用性
用写入吞吐换读延迟
没有代价，纯粹是收益
用存储空间换查询性能
options_en: Trading consistency for availability.
Trading write throughput for read latency.
No cost at all, pure upside.
Trading storage space for query speed.
why: 同一份数据按多种粒度多存几份，换来常见查询直接命中汇总行。多花的是存储和维护成本，性质与缓存同源。
why_en: Pre-aggregated rollup tables trade extra storage for faster common queries, which is essentially a form of caching.
tradeoff: 存储空间 vs 常见查询的响应速度

termDefinitions.meaning: 在已有明细表基础上，按更粗粒度（天/周）再聚合出的表，用来加速大范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup table re-aggregates existing detail data at a coarser grain like day or week to speed up wide-range queries.

optionExplanations: rollup 不涉及跨副本的可用性权衡，这不是本题要讨论的取舍轴。
rollup 写入发生在夜间批处理，不占用主链路的写入吞吐，真正的代价不在这里。
任何预计算都要为存储和维护买单，说没有代价违反了常识。
本质是拿存储空间换查询速度：把同一批数据按不同粒度多备份几份，常见查询就能直接命中现成的汇总行，代价是多花的存储和维护，跟缓存是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Rollups don't involve a cross-replica availability tradeoff — that's not the axis at play here.
Rollup writes happen in a nightly batch, not on the main write path, so write throughput isn't actually what's being spent.
Any precomputation has to be paid for in storage and upkeep — claiming it's free contradicts the basics.

The core trade: store the same data again at several granularities so that everyday queries can land straight on a ready-made rollup — the price is extra storage and upkeep, exactly what a cache trades too.

q: 把「不丢任何点击数据」的防线按文章叙述顺序排列：
q_en: Put the defenses for not losing click data in the order described by the article.
steps: 小窗口不依赖 checkpoint：Flink 挂了最多重算 1 分钟的聚合
数据湖归档 + 每日 Spark 对账，兜底纠正一切细微偏差
流本身多副本：Kafka 跨 broker、Kinesis 跨可用区复制，抗节点故障
开启 7 天持久保留：处理器宕机后可从流中重放漏掉的事件
why: 四道防线层层递进：副本抗单点、保留期供重放、小窗口让重算便宜、对账做最终兜底。前两道同属流层配置，先后可互换。
why_en: The defenses stack: replication and retention give you replay, tiny windows make reprocessing cheap, and daily reconciliation is the final safety net.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理器定期把内部状态写到持久存储，故障后可以从最近一次检查点恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is a periodic snapshot of a stream processor's state written to durable storage so it can resume after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息队列保存历史事件的时长，在此期间可以重新读取或重放数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retention is how long a message queue keeps historical events available for replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放原始未加工数据的低成本存储，常用对象存储实现，供后续批处理读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data lake is low-cost storage for raw, unprocessed data, typically object storage, used later by batch jobs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式批处理计算引擎，常用来做离线的大规模数据重新聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spark is a distributed batch-processing engine commonly used for large-scale offline re-aggregation.

scenario: 45 分钟面试，中级候选人的时间只够走完高层设计加一两轮追问。
scenario_en: In 45 minutes a mid-level candidate only has time for the high-level design plus a follow-up or two.
q: 中级（E4）候选人在这道题上的达标线是什么？
q_en: What is the passing bar for a mid-level (E4) candidate on this problem?
options: 给出完整的 Lambda 架构和热分片打散方案
理解需要预聚合、能提批处理方案、追问下能推理解题
只需要画出单库方案
背出 Kinesis 的分片限额
options_en: Deliver a complete Lambda architecture with hot-shard splitting.
Understands pre-aggregation is needed, proposes a batch solution, and reasons well when probed.
Just sketch a single-database design.
Recite Kinesis's shard limits from memory.
why: 中级重广度（约 80/20）：能搭出满足功能需求的高层设计、理解预聚合的必要性，面对追问能现场推理即可，不要求完整容错方案。
why_en: A mid-level candidate should recognize the need for pre-aggregation, propose at least a batch solution, and reason well under probing about idempotency and database choices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时跑批处理层和实时流处理层，用批处理结果纠正流处理误差的架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lambda architecture runs both a batch layer and a real-time streaming layer, using the batch results to correct streaming errors.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS Kinesis 单个分片每秒最多处理 1MB 或 1000 条记录的硬性限制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kinesis shard is hard-capped at about one megabyte or one thousand records per second.

optionExplanations: 要求交付完整容错架构和热点打散方案，超出了中级候选人的达标线，那是 Staff+ 才被期待的深度。
理解需要预聚合、能提出批处理方案、面对追问能现场推理，这正是文章给中级候选人划的及格线。
只画未预聚合的单库方案，连需要预聚合的认识都没体现，达不到中级要求。
背出具体产品的分片限额考的是记忆而不是设计推理，追问下背数字不等于理解为什么要分片。
optionExplanations_en: Expecting a full fault-tolerant architecture and hot-partition mitigation overshoots the mid-level bar — that's Staff+-level depth.
Recognizing the need for pre-aggregation, proposing a batch approach, and reasoning it out under follow-up questions is exactly the bar set for a mid-level candidate.
Sketching only a non-pre-aggregated single-database design doesn't even show awareness that pre-aggregation is needed — falls short of the bar.
Reciting a specific product's shard limit tests memorization, not design reasoning — knowing the number under a follow-up doesn't mean understanding why sharding matters.

scenario: 同一道题分别面 E5 和 Staff+，45 分钟里广度和深度的时间分配不同。
scenario_en: The same problem is asked of an E5 and a Staff+ candidate, and the 45 minutes get split differently between breadth and depth.
q: 资深（E5）与 Staff+ 在这道题上的期望差异是什么？
q_en: How do expectations differ between Senior (E5) and Staff+ candidates on this problem?
options: 资深深挖扩展与容错、对比批流；Staff+ 还要给方案和实战经验
资深阶段只考察设计广度，Staff+ 只考察技术深度
无论候选人级别如何，面试官的期望标准完全一致
Staff+ 候选人可以跳过高层设计直接进入深挖
options_en: Senior digs into scaling, fault tolerance, and batch-vs-stream; Staff+ also brings a concrete design and hard-won experience.
Senior is tested only on breadth, Staff+ only on depth.
The bar is exactly the same regardless of level.
Staff+ candidates can skip the high-level design entirely.
why: 资深约 60/40、Staff 约 40/60（广度/深度）：级别越高越要主动发现问题、驱动深挖，并用实践经验支撑技术权衡。
why_en: Senior speeds through the high-level design to dig into scaling and fault tolerance; Staff+ goes deeper on trade-offs and can teach the interviewer something new.
tradeoff: 资深：广度优先、快速收敛到深挖 vs Staff+：深度优先、驱动整场对话
optionExplanations: 资深候选人快速带过高层设计，重点深挖扩展性与容错并对比批流；Staff+ 要更深，能给出具体容错方案、并用实践经验反哺权衡。
两级都是广度加深度的组合，只是比例不同，说资深只看广度、Staff+只看深度是过度简化。
两级在深挖程度和主动驱动对话的程度上明确不同，说标准完全一致与文章描述矛盾。
Staff+ 是快速带过高层设计而不是跳过，仍要过一遍整体架构再深入。
optionExplanations_en: A senior candidate moves quickly through the high-level design and focuses the depth on scaling, fault tolerance, and batch-vs-stream tradeoffs; Staff+ goes further, offering concrete fault-tolerance designs backed by real experience.
Both levels blend breadth and depth, just in different ratios — saying senior is breadth-only and Staff+ is depth-only oversimplifies it.
The two levels clearly differ in how deep they're expected to dig and how much they drive the conversation — claiming identical standards contradicts that.
Staff+ moves quickly through the high-level design rather than skipping it — they still need to walk through the overall architecture before going deep.
